modules.title: Your first CAPL event
modules.description: Start an ECU and distinguish logs from traffic.
modules.task: Write an on start event that prints exactly one message: ECU ready

theory.title: CAN frames and CAPL transmission
theory.text: CANoe analyzes and simulates networks. CAPL reacts to events. Our app is an educational subset, not Vector CANoe or a CAPL compiler.

theory.title: Startup
theory.text: on start runs once when measurement starts. In our lab Start simulation begins a fresh replay; clicking a key dispatches a different event.

theory.title: Logs versus frames
theory.text: write() adds text to the Write window. output(message) submits a frame for transmission. A log saying 'sent' is not evidence that a frame was transmitted.

theory.title: CANoe workflow
theory.text: Configure a node in Simulation Setup, compile its CAPL, start measurement, then inspect Write and Trace. Graphics is useful for signal trends. This app has no physical CAN hardware or arbitration simulation.

theory.title: Interview reasoning
theory.text: Investigate preconditions → stimulus → communication → timing → verdict. A frame visible in Trace does not establish ECU application acceptance.

theory.title: CRC versus sequence
theory.text: A valid application CRC does not prove that a counter sequence is acceptable. If duplicates are forbidden, 5,6,7,7,8 fails the sequence rule. Our later E2E lab states its own modulo-16 toy rules explicitly.

theory.title: Response deadlines
theory.text: For an ACC response required within 100 ms, wait for a fresh qualifying ACTIVE observation with that deadline. An immediate read may be stale, while a fixed delay alone does not establish a correct verdict.

modules.challenge: Start with exactly two logs: ECU booting, then ECU ready.

theory.title: Execution order
theory.text: Statements in a handler run sequentially. Their order matters for logs, byte assignments and output snapshots.

theory.title: Snapshots
theory.text: output() captures the payload at that call. Later assignments do not alter a previously captured transmission.

theory.title: Test evidence
theory.text: An exact sequence check rejects extra entries and reversed order. Match the requirement rather than checking whether the expected text appears somewhere.

theory.title: Event selection
theory.text: on key 'a' runs for lowercase a. Starting measurement does not execute this handler. Key A and key a differ.

theory.title: CANoe interaction
theory.text: In CANoe, keyboard events require keyboard input reaching the measurement environment. Our Press A button explicitly dispatches lowercase a.

theory.title: Isolation
theory.text: The basic Run operation is stateless. The advanced virtual-clock lab replays a history to preserve state across actions. Editing code starts a new history.

modules.title: Transmit vehicle speed
modules.description: Build real payload evidence for the 100 → 50 km/h exercise.
modules.task: On key a, transmit exactly two ID 0x123 frames, DLC 2: 10 27 then 88 13. Logs alone do not pass.

theory.title: Classical standard CAN
theory.text: Standard data identifiers are 11 bits, 0x000–0x7FF; Classical CAN carries 0–8 bytes. Between competing standard data frames a lower numeric ID wins arbitration. An ID is not a destination address.

theory.title: Signal definition
theory.text: Our speed occupies bytes 0–1, unsigned little-endian, factor 0.01 km/h and offset 0. This is our own definition, not a universal CAN rule.
theory.example:
raw = byte0 + 256 × byte1
physical = raw × factor + offset
10 27 → 10000 → 100 km/h
88 13 → 5000 → 50 km/h

theory.title: CAPL transmission
theory.text: Declare the message, set its DLC and bytes, then call output(). Use Trace for Tx evidence and Write for text logs. Our simulated Tx has no physical bus ACK or arbitration.

modules.challenge: On key a, send ID 0x123, DLC 2, for 25 km/h then 75 km/h. No extra transmissions.

modules.title: Multiple events and state
modules.description: Initialize once, then update persistent state on input.
modules.task: Initialize Status DLC in on start. Each a increments count and transmits ID 0x200 with count in its one-byte payload: 1,2,3.

theory.title: State lifetime
theory.text: Global values persist during a measurement. on start initializes them; each key handler uses the updated value. Resetting the virtual simulation starts from declarations again.

theory.title: Replay model
theory.text: The browser submits code plus action history. The server deterministically rebuilds state from time zero. State is not shared with other browser tabs and is not a database record.

theory.title: Multiple handlers
theory.text: Several events may coexist. The supported interpreter allows integer/byte scalars, message objects, if/else, arithmetic, comparisons, and declared msTimer timers. It has no loops, custom functions, arrays or general CAPL compiler.

modules.title: Timers and periodic traffic
modules.description: Reschedule a one-shot timer to produce periodic messages.
modules.task: Transmit ID 0x300 data 01 at 100,200,300 ms. Key s cancels the timer. Key r restarts after a fresh 100 ms.

theory.title: One-shot timers
theory.text: An msTimer expires once. Periodic transmission requires setTimer in its handler. Calling setTimer again replaces the timer's next due time; cancelTimer removes it.

theory.title: Virtual time
theory.text: Advance time runs all due timers in timestamp order. At equal timestamps timers use scheduling order. A timer due at the advance boundary fires before the next key or receive action. This is our explicit lab rule, not a universal CANoe scheduling guarantee.

theory.title: Trace evidence
theory.text: Inspect successive Tx timestamps. A 100 ms requirement means a 100 ms interval, not merely three frames. No wall-clock sleeping is used.

modules.challenge: Use a 50 ms period with the same stop/restart keys. Check both first delay and repeat interval.

modules.title: Reception and watchdogs
modules.description: Detect silence after the last received message.
modules.task: Arm a 500 ms watchdog at startup; rearm on each 0x300 reception. Log Communication timeout once after silence; receiving again clears timedOut.

theory.title: Reception
theory.text: on message 0x300 responds to injected Rx frames. Our own Tx frames do not automatically loop back into reception. this.byte(index) is read-only and guarded by received DLC.

theory.title: Watchdog
theory.text: If the final reception is at 200 ms and timeout is 500 ms, expiry is at 700 ms. A flag set once cannot monitor later loss. Rearm on reception rather than merely arming once at startup.

theory.title: Recovery and boundaries
theory.text: The lab sets timedOut=0 on reception and 1 on expiry. An Rx action after advancing exactly to a timer deadline occurs after that timer fired; design boundary checks accordingly.

modules.challenge: Implement the same watchdog with a 300 ms timeout and recovery.

modules.title: Signals and DBC
modules.description: Decode bytes with a stated signal definition.
modules.task: Configure an unsigned two-byte signal at byte 0 so 10 27 decodes to 100 km/h and 88 13 to 50 km/h.

theory.title: DBC fields
theory.text: A signal definition specifies start bit, bit length, byte order, signedness, factor, offset and unit. The supplied VehicleSpeed.dbc has a 16-bit little-endian signal starting at bit 0.

theory.title: Conversion
theory.text: physical = raw × factor + offset. Intel little-endian means the first byte contains the least significant part for this byte-aligned example. Motorola DBC start-bit numbering has additional rules; our decoder supports only byte-aligned unsigned fields, not arbitrary DBC parsing.

theory.title: Debugging
theory.text: Wrong byte order, wrong factor or wrong offset can produce plausible but incorrect values. Validate at several known values, including boundaries.
theory.example:
100 km/h → raw 10000 → bytes 10 27
50 km/h → raw 5000 → bytes 88 13

modules.challenge: Decode a big-endian two-byte field with factor 0.1 and offset -10; validate 03 E8 → 90 and 01 F4 → 40.

modules.title: E2E integrity and sequence
modules.description: Separate CRC integrity from counter acceptance.
modules.task: Classify each frame under the stated modulo-16 teaching profile with zero lost-frame tolerance.

theory.title: Two CRC layers
theory.text: CAN's link-layer CRC differs from an application CRC carried in the payload. An application CRC can pass while the receiver rejects a repeated or out-of-window counter.

theory.title: Teaching profile
theory.text: Our explicit toy profile uses modulo 16, a two-byte big-endian Data ID, one counter byte and supplied data bytes. CRC-8 uses polynomial 0x1D, init 0xFF, no reflection, xorout 0xFF. This is not an AUTOSAR E2E profile or certification implementation.

theory.title: Acceptance
theory.text: The first good CRC establishes the accepted baseline. Delta=(counter-lastAccepted) modulo 16. Delta 0 is REPEATED. Delta 1 is OK. Deltas up to maxLost+1 are OK_SOME_LOST; larger deltas are WRONG_SEQUENCE. Rejected frames do not advance our accepted baseline.

theory.title: Investigate
theory.text: Inspect payload, counter, application CRC and timestamps. Consider two transmitters with the same ID or a replay. Never assume all 4-bit AUTOSAR counters wrap modulo 16; actual rules are profile-specific.
theory.example:
Toy example: 15 → 0 is delta 1
5 → 6 → 7 → 7 → 8 contains a repeated 7

modules.challenge: Classify a new sequence with maxLost=1. Include duplicate, bad CRC, loss tolerance, and recovery.

modules.title: Test verdicts and deadlines
modules.description: Verify the required response rather than a stale state.
modules.task: Select event-based checking with a 100 ms deadline. It must accept 80 ms, reject 120 ms and reject no response.

theory.title: Test structure
theory.text: Preconditions → stimulus → bounded response wait → verification → verdict. A missing precondition makes this lab NOT_EXECUTED; it is not evidence that the ECU passed or failed.

theory.title: Fresh observations
theory.text: Observations are timestamped relative to the command. This lab treats supplied samples as fresh observations, not cached states from before the stimulus. At the deadline, an observation exactly at the boundary is accepted by our stated requirement.

theory.title: CAPL Test Modules
theory.text: CANoe test functions include bounded waits and verdict reporting. write("PASS") is merely a log; testStepPass/testStepFail affect reports. These functions are discussed in theory; this app's Test Bench is a separate teaching model, not a CAPL Test Module interpreter.

theory.title: ACC false failures
theory.text: If activation arrives at 80 ms within a 100 ms requirement, an immediate read can fail incorrectly. A 500 ms delay also does not prove the deadline was respected.

modules.challenge: Use the same approach for a 150 ms deadline; cover boundary, late, absent and invalid-setup cases.

modules.title: ADAS scenario reasoning
modules.description: Connect trace evidence to ACC and AEB requirements.
modules.task: Classify braking decisions for the four simplified AEB cases under the stated 2-second TTC threshold.

theory.title: Abbreviations
theory.text: ADAS: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems. ACC: Adaptive Cruise Control. AEB: Automatic Emergency Braking. FCW: Forward Collision Warning. TTC: Time To Collision. HIL/SIL/MIL: Hardware/Software/Model in the Loop.

theory.title: TTC model
theory.text: For constant velocities on the same path with positive closing speed: TTC=distance/closingSpeed. Convert km/h to m/s by dividing by 3.6. If there is no positive closing speed, this model has no finite collision time.

theory.title: Explicit AEB rule
theory.text: This lab requests braking only when sensors are valid, an obstacle is on path, closing speed is positive, and TTC ≤ configured threshold. Invalid sensors produce DEGRADED. This is a deliberately simplified offline teaching model, not a production control algorithm or driving guidance.

theory.title: ACC model
theory.text: Our state demonstration is OFF when disabled, DEGRADED with invalid sensing, OVERRIDDEN with driver braking and ACTIVE otherwise. Actual activation conditions, priorities and fallback behavior are OEM-specific.

theory.title: Failure investigation
theory.text: False positive: intervention without the specified hazard. False negative: missing required intervention. Define the requirement and timing before judging either. Expand real validation with sensor uncertainty, cut-in/out, stationary targets, curves and driver override.

modules.challenge: Classify four new cases at a 1.5-second threshold, including no closing speed and an invalid sensor.

foundation.prompt: Which statement transmits a CAN message?
foundation.explanation: output() transmits; write() logs text. Assignments only change the message object.

foundation.prompt: Decode 88 13 as unsigned little-endian speed, factor 0.01, offset 0.
Where do you inspect CAN identifiers, payloads and timestamps in CANoe?
foundation.explanation: Trace displays communication events. Write displays CAPL text logs.

foundation.prompt: Counters are 5,6,7,7,8; all CRCs pass. Duplicates are forbidden. Is this valid?
options: Yes, because every CRC is valid
Yes, because the final counter is 8
foundation.explanation: CRC and sequence checks are distinct. A repeated counter violates this stated requirement.

foundation.prompt: ACC must activate within 100 ms. What should the test do?
options: Check the state immediately and fail if inactive
Wait 500 ms and always report PASS
Wait for the required active state with a 100 ms deadline
foundation.explanation: Wait for a fresh qualifying response within the requirement's deadline.
